_comment: Coding-task decomposition ladder for issue #847. EVERY task is real work from a real open Formal AI issue that has never had a pull request, decomposed L1 (whole issue -> PR) down to L4 (one atomic edit). No synthetic toy tasks: the point is to teach Formal AI to code on the work we actually need done, so a passing L4 is a real contribution and not a throwaway. Driven through `formal-ai with agent`, i.e. the exact path Hive Mind uses (link-assistant/hive-mind#2059).
corpus_note: Seeds drawn from the 43 open formal-ai issues with no PR on any branch, so an attempt cannot collide with in-flight work.
verification_note: `verify` runs in the repository root after the agent finishes. Tasks are ordered so a level-N task's precondition is the repo's real current state, not the output of another task. Mutating tasks are reverted by the runner via `git checkout -- .` so every task starts from a clean tree.

levels.1: Whole issue -> pull request (the Hive Mind `solve` shape).
levels.2: One coherent deliverable of that issue.
levels.4: One atomic operation on one named file.

tasks.prompt: Solve GitHub issue https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/846 in this repository and open a pull request with the fix.
tasks.verify: git log --oneline -1 --all | grep -qi "846" && git branch -a | grep -q "issue-846"
tasks.note: Ceiling. Whole issue -> PR. Records the gap between what Hive Mind will ask for and what is currently possible. Verified by the existence of a real branch/PR, not by narration: `verify: true` made this unfalsifiable in the first run and it scored a false PASS.

tasks.prompt: In this repository, add a paths-ignore filter for experiments/**, dev/log/** and docs/case-studies/** to the push trigger of .github/workflows/release.yml so that commits touching only those folders do not run the pipeline.
tasks.note: One coherent deliverable of #846: the workflow-level fix.

tasks.prompt: In scripts/detect-code-changes.rs, the docs-changed output is computed from the .md file extension alone and ignores the excluded_folders list. Change it so files inside excluded folders do not set docs-changed.
tasks.verify: grep -n 'docs_changed' scripts/detect-code-changes.rs | grep -qv 'has_extension(f, "md")' && ! grep -q 'let docs_changed = changed_files.iter().any(|f| has_extension(f, "md"));' scripts/detect-code-changes.rs
tasks.note: One concrete edit with the file and the defect named. This is the smallest genuinely useful fix in #846.

tasks.prompt: In this repository, read scripts/detect-code-changes.rs and tell me every folder listed in the excluded_folders array.
tasks.note: Atomic read against the real file #846 changes. Read-only floor: if this fails, no coding task above it is reachable.

tasks.prompt: In the file scripts/detect-code-changes.rs, add "dev/log/" to the excluded_folders array.
tasks.note: Atomic single-string edit to a real source file, on the exact array #846 is about.

tasks.prompt: Solve GitHub issue https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/843 in this repository and open a pull request with the fix.
tasks.note: Second ceiling case, against a reasoning-core issue rather than a CI issue. Verified by the existence of a real branch/PR, not by narration: `verify: true` made this unfalsifiable in the first run and it scored a false PASS.

tasks.prompt: In src/solver.rs, the function record_external_search emits a fabricated source:http evidence link pointing at https://example.org with a sha256 of the prompt. Remove that fabricated source:http and cache_hit emission so no fake provenance is recorded.
tasks.note: The single highest-value edit in #843, with file and function named.

tasks.prompt: In this repository, find where the string example.org is emitted as evidence and tell me the file and function name.
tasks.note: Atomic search on the real defect. Precondition for 843.L3.

tasks.prompt: Create a new Rust module file src/si_units.rs in this repository containing a public function millimetres_to_metres that takes an f64 and returns it divided by 1000.0, plus a unit test asserting millimetres_to_metres(1000.0) equals 1.0.
tasks.verify: test -f src/si_units.rs && grep -q 'fn millimetres_to_metres' src/si_units.rs && grep -q '#\[test\]' src/si_units.rs
tasks.note: First real deliverable of #700 (universal measuring units): a new module plus its test, in the repo's own conventions.

tasks.prompt: Create a new file src/si_units.rs in this repository containing exactly one public Rust function named millimetres_to_metres that takes an f64 and returns that value divided by 1000.0.
tasks.verify: test -f src/si_units.rs && grep -q 'pub fn millimetres_to_metres' src/si_units.rs
tasks.note: The same #700 deliverable with the test half removed - isolates whether composition or code generation is the failure.

tasks.prompt: In REQUIREMENTS.md, find the row for requirement R67 and report its current implementation status verbatim.
tasks.note: #710 is largely REQUIREMENTS.md status reconciliation; this is the read step that every such fix starts from.

tasks.prompt: Split this coding task into at least two smaller independent subtasks and list them as a numbered list, nothing else: 'Add a paths-ignore filter for experiments/** to the push trigger in .github/workflows/release.yml and make docs-changed in scripts/detect-code-changes.rs respect the excluded_folders list.'
tasks.note: Decomposition itself as a task. If Formal AI cannot split a task it cannot drive its own ladder, so this is a prerequisite capability rather than a nice-to-have. Tracked separately.

tasks.prompt: Answer with one word, yes or no: is the following coding task already atomic, meaning it cannot be usefully split further? 'In the file scripts/detect-code-changes.rs, add "dev/log/" to the excluded_folders array.'
tasks.note: The termination test for recursive decomposition: knowing when to stop splitting.
